title: Multi-DoF Force Characterization of Soft Actuators
observation: A configurable planar fixture measures external interactions under pulling, tip loading and three-point bending. Four-pressure pulling curves and fitted tip force maps distinguish boundary-condition effects. Figure 10 compares neutral configurations at 150 kPa to minima of fitted force magnitude.
rights: IEEE article; public author copy inspected. Link, citation and original factual summary only.
limitations: Three two-axis load modules measure fixture reactions. Neither motor currents nor a co-located six-axis wrist sensor were reported.

title: Stretchable Materials for Robust Soft Actuators towards Assistive Wearable Devices
authors: Gunjan Agarwal; Nicolas Besuchet; Basile Audergon; Jamie Paik
version: PMC5037455.1 JATS, Scientific Reports version of record
observation: Separate free-displacement and blocked-load experiments compare shell-reinforced soft linear and bending actuators with finite-element predictions. The linear actuator characterization steps pressure from 0 to 45 kPa over 10–15 s. Three repeats per geometric variant assess positioning and pressure-angle repeatability.
limitations: Endpoint blocking and free motion impose different mechanical boundary conditions. This cited study does not provide the 2019 Zenodo trial files.

title: Soft Pneumatic Actuator Fascicles for High Force and Reliability
authors: Matthew A. Robertson; Hamed Sadeghi; Juan Manuel Florez; Jamie Paik
locator: Figs. 5(c,d) and 7; discussion of individual versus platform tests
observation: Four actuator packs at 2 bar produce greater than 432 N blocked platform force against a single-axis 600 N load cell. The test authors attribute differing per-module estimates to constraints on buckling. The closed-loop tracking case uses platform angle from an IMU.
limitations: Measured force depends on fixture constraints. A pressure rating is not an observed saturation transition. See the 2019 equation-sign correction.

title: Correction to: Soft Pneumatic Actuator Fascicles for High Force and Reliability by Robertson MA, Sadeghi H, Florez JM, Paik J. Soft Robot 2017;4:23–32. DOI: 10.1089/soro.2016.0029
authors: No named author (Soft Robotics publisher correction)
version: Soft Robotics 6(5), p.685, PMC full correction
observation: The first term of the force expression for the extending actuators requires a minus sign. The authors report that all calculations and figures already used the corrected expression.
rights: Public PMC correction; linked and summarized.
limitations: Amends one publication. No new experiment or raw data.

title: Towards Plug-n-Play numerical control for Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems
authors: Vuk Lesi; Zivana Jakovljevic; Miroslav Pajic
observation: Uses timing errors measured on hardware to drive a software-in-the-loop two-axis toolpath comparison against ISO 10791-7 tolerances. Separates controller timing measurements from simulated feature geometry.
rights: IEEE article; public author copy inspected. Link, citation and original factual summary only.
limitations: The simulated toolpath and measured switching times are different evidence. No packet trace or independent surface measurement was verified.

title: Synchronization of Distributed Controllers in Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Vuk Lesi; Zivana Jakovljevic; Miroslav Pajic
locator: Figs. 5 and 9(a–c); Tables in machining comparison
observation: Two physical low-level controllers run interpolators at a 1 ms period. Figure 9 reports timing alignment of ±1.6 µs with the TCP server offline and ±3.4 µs when following a trajectory supplied by the server. The paper separately treats alignment of actuation pulses.
rights: IEEE article; public author copy inspected. Link, citation and original factual summary only.
limitations: Scope traces concern interpolator invocation. A recorded XY trajectory alone cannot reconstruct individual clock or packet events.

title: Distributing Numerical Control for Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems
authors: Vuk Lesi; Zivana Jakovljevic; Miroslav Pajic
version: Undated Duke manuscript. Cited as Technical Report (2022) by Zenodo 6399688, reference [3].
locator: Tables III–IV; tests using feedback signals
observation: Physical stage experiments compare synchronous and distributed numerical control. The authors use local encoder feedback to estimate diagonal accuracy/repeatability and no-load geometric deviations. The manufacturer’s individual-axis repeatability rating is ±10 µm.
rights: Public Duke author manuscript; redistribution terms unverified.
limitations: An independent interferometer was not used. Year comes from source dataset citation, not publication registration; no journal DOI was established.

title: GAN-based Data Augmentation in the Design of Cyber-attack Detection Methods
observation: Documents the normal-operation acquisition chain between controller and electro-pneumatic regulator. The authors measured 399,000 DAQ voltage samples at 100 Hz; Fig. 5 shows a 1,500-sample excerpt.
rights: Public IcETRAN proceedings; files not redistributed.
limitations: Adjacent rig description. This single count does not identify it as one of the 12 Zenodo 4556924 files. Only normal physical signal acquisition was considered.

title: Detection of cyber-attacks in electro-pneumatic positioning system with distributed control
authors: Dusan M. Nedeljkovic; Zivana B. Jakovljevic; Zoran Dj. Miljkovic; Miroslav Pajic
observation: The Belgrade repository explicitly cites this paper for the architecture of the electro-pneumatic positioner; use as a bibliographic lead for the physical rig.
rights: Public Crossref metadata; bibliographic facts and link.
limitations: No publication full text used for a quantitative claim. The architecture citation alone does not establish shard identity.

title: Iterative control in automotive testing
authors: N. C. Hay; D. E. Roberts
